title: Understanding Users' Content Contribution Behavior When Knowledge Can Be Priced
authors: Ziwei Cong; Zhao Ying; Zilei Zhang
near_miss_reason: Nonlinear model: all main-text estimates (Table 2 onward) are Poisson; the linear after_enroll columns are robustness checks in Online Appendix B.3 (article checked Nov 2, 2026).
eligible_reason: Zhihu user-week panel around the launch of paid live sessions (Zhihu Live, announcement week 2016-19). Two treatment definitions: (a) if_speaker x after, with after = common announcement date (single-date DiD, not staggered); (b) after_enroll = after_{it}, which switches on at each participant's own first event week. In the shipped panel after_enroll is binary and absorbing, 133 participants enroll across 50 distinct calendar weeks (diff_week 1 to 46+), all have pre-periods, and 4,867 nonparticipants are never treated. The headline estimator is xtpoisson FE (nonlinear, excluded). The 'Different functional forms' robustness block reports linear xtreg FE versions with user FE (xtset member_id) and calendar-week dummies (weekb58-weeka56; diff_week is calendar time because intervention_week is 2016-19 for everyone), no controls, clustered by member_id. With user FE, if_speaker is absorbed and 1.after_enroll and 1.if_speaker#1.after_enroll are collinear (after_enroll is nonzero only for participants), so the regression reduces to a staggered binary TWFE in after_enroll. The two after_enroll linear columns qualify. Their placement (main-text robustness table vs Web Appendix) cannot be verified without the article.
design_notes: Stata. diff-in-diffs.do on main.csv (5,000 users x 117 weeks = 585,000 rows). Main effect: xtpoisson answer_num_week i.if_speaker##i.after weekb58-weeka56, fe vce(robust) and the same with after_enroll (lines ~150-165). Robustness block (outreg2 main_effect_rb.xls): xtpoisson + tenure control; xtreg ln/level with after (lines 266, 270, single-date); xtreg ln/level with after_enroll (lines 278, 282, staggered); xtpoisson sample restrictions (no_activity_after14/30, no_other_activity_post, answer_num_total<1181). Falsification (falsi_b26-b31) and relative-time model are Poisson and relative to the common announcement week. Matched-sample (match1, section 4.6.3) versions are Poisson only. duration_analysis.do: xtpoisson with abs_dis_create (continuous distance to event creation). promotional_effect.do: cross-sectional event-level regressions.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Distinct first after_enroll weeks among the 133 participants in the shipped 5,000-user subsample.

specs.treatment_var: after_enroll (written as i.if_speaker##i.after_enroll; if_speaker absorbed by user FE, interaction collinear with after_enroll)
specs.treatment_definition: after_{it}: 1 from the participant's own enrollment (first live event) week onward; 0 for all nonparticipants
specs.time_var: diff_week (calendar week relative to the common announcement week 2016-19)
specs.reported_location: Online Appendix B.3 (not main text; confirmed from the published PDF)
specs.notes: Shipped data are a random 5,000-user subsample of the original panel, so published coefficients will not match exactly.

specs.reported_location: Online Appendix B.3 (not main text; confirmed from the published PDF)

excluded_specs_summary: Headline xtpoisson FE columns (nonlinear); all if_speaker x after columns (single common date); Poisson relative-time model; matched-sample Poisson; tenure-control Poisson; duration analysis with continuous abs_dis_create.
data_provenance_note: README: 'We randomly sampled a subset of 5000 users (133 participants and 4867 from the original dataset used in the paper)'. Member IDs are deliberately inconsistent across files.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Eligible only through the two linear after_enroll robustness columns; the paper's headline estimates are Poisson. Needs an article check that the functional-form robustness table is in the main text (the README places section 4.6.3 matched-sample analysis in the main text with balance in Table W2, so section 4.6 robustness is likely main text). Exact replication impossible because the package ships a random subsample. | Main session, Nov 2 2026: published PDF checked; functional-form robustness is in Online Appendix B.3, so no main-text specification qualifies (near miss: nonlinear model).
